sample_output.query: Can an MCP host trust tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint) to skip user confirmation? What does the spec actually require?
sample_output.tldr: No. Annotations are a risk vocabulary, not a permission system. Defaults are pessimistic; from an untrusted server they are informational only. Skip confirmation only for servers you already trust, and keep enforcement in the host (consent, sandbox, egress).

body.what_annotations_are: Tool annotations shipped in spec revision 2025-03-26. Fields: readOnlyHint (default false), destructiveHint (default true), idempotentHint (default false), openWorldHint (default true). Every property is a hint.
body.trust_rule: Clients MUST treat annotations as untrusted unless the server is trusted. A server can lie (readOnlyHint: true and still delete files).
body.unannotated_defaults: Unannotated tool = assume write, destructive, non-idempotent, open-world.
body.tool_safety: MCP Tool Safety: tool descriptions/annotations are untrusted unless the server is trusted; hosts must get explicit user consent before invoking a tool.
body.real_guarantees: Consent UI, sandbox, and network egress controls — not booleans from the server.
body.recommendation: Do not auto-approve solely on readOnlyHint from a third-party server.
